newsitem.title: DUBAI: Islamic insurance market seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Islamic insurance market seen growing.

text.p: The Islamic insurance market is forecast to be worth $2.1 billion worldwide by the year 2010, one of the Arab world's biggest insurers said.
Ajmal Bhatty of the Bahrain-based Arab Insurance Group (ARIG) said $1.6 billion of this would be in non-life policies.

He told a conference on Islamic banking in Dubai that about $300 million in Islamic insurance premiums are written annually in Arab countries with $70 million in Asian Pacific countries and $5 million in Turkey.
Bhatty said nearly 30 takaful companies operate in the Arab world, out of a total 50 across the world.

Under takaful, which literally means helping one another, insurance is provided in conformity with Islamic principles. Under Islam's sharia principles, business should be done on the basis of sale and purchase of assets. Giving loans by charging interest is considered usury.

Bhatty said the growth of Islamic insurance in the Middle East has been hampered by socio-cultural reasons, including "cultural resistance towards insurance...for example protection was seen to be afforded by the extended family system driven by patriarchal controls".
He said Gulf Arab states, where governments have put a squeeze on spending, have the best potential for developing Islamic insurance.

"Governments in the Gulf are finding it increasingly difficult to maintain their position as the largest employer...(so) the social and commercial role of insurance is increasingly being recognised as a pre-requisite for the economic strength of the individual and corporations," he said.
Bahrain-based ARIG is one of the biggest insurers in the Arab world and is equally owned by the governments of Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Libya.
